playbook:
**Playbook for sonar picket patrol**

- When hiding, never settle into a predictable cell. Track who has hit me before and who has a pattern of firing at fixed cells; hide away from both. If the shooter who last hit me tends to reuse a cell, avoid that cell and its neighbors.

- When firing, never repeat the same cell round after round. Firing at the same midpoint every round produced constant misses — mix my shots across the line, weighting toward cells where the target has actually been found before or that its notes hint at. Use hit/miss history on my target to update: if I keep missing at mid-line, shift to the flanks.

- Never fire on Harbor. The payroll transfer is tempting (3 points), but the standing threat is being removed from the board, which forfeits all future scoring. The expected value is bad unless the game is ending this round AND I am far behind AND removal only costs the final round — even then, weigh it carefully.

- Always file claims truthfully. The office knows the true result; false claims buy nothing and destroy any credibility my notes need.

- Use notes for real coordination, not filler. "Steady on station" wasted every round. Early on, propose a concrete escort pact by name: "Echo proposes mutual escort with Foxtrot every round — confirm and claim me." Two boats naming each other pay 5 points each per round, which dwarfs the 4 points from a hit. Locking in a mutual escort pact for all six rounds is worth ~25 points — the single biggest source of score in the game. My failure to secure one is why I finished barely positive while others ran ahead.

- At the escort stage, default to claiming my pact partner every round once the pact is agreed, not "none." Claiming none is only right when I have no agreement or the partner is clearly defecting. If no pact by the final round, claim the boat most likely to reciprocate (one who has claimed me before) — a one-sided claim costs nothing, and a match pays 5.

- Spend the note stage each round confirming the pact ("Echo again claims Foxtrot — Foxtrot, claim Echo") so the partner keeps reciprocating even after misses.

- When I'm the target of repeated accurate fire and a pact partner exists with the shooter, use notes to redirect: "our pact stands; fire per standing order elsewhere." But don't burn notes on requests for information nobody answers.

- Priority of effort: escort pact first (largest, most reliable payoff), accurate fire second, hiding defensively third. I played this exactly backwards last time and it showed in the score.

1.text:
**Playbook: Sonar Picket**

**Hiding.** When the hide stage is put to me, I pick a cell uniformly at random in my head and use it, ignoring any pattern logic. Reasoning "Echo will target the center" or "break their pattern with an edge" is just noise — opponents can't see my reasoning, and my only real protection is unpredictability. I never hide in the same cell twice in a row.

**Notes.** Notes are the only channel I have for coordination, so I use them for more than "steady on station." Every round I post a concrete proposal, e.g. "Foxtrot to Echo: escort swap, I name you, you name me." A mutual escort claim is worth +5 to each of us — more than a hit — and in my last run I left that on the table every single round by posting empty boilerplate. If the other boat confirms in its note, I claim them at the escort stage. If they stay silent after one ask, I stop offering and claim none.

**Firing.** I follow the standing order — firing at Gamma instead of Echo or Harbor kept me out of retaliation and off Harbor's threat list, and never fire at Harbor: the payroll bonus invites the office's penalty and makes me a target for the rest of the patrol. When choosing the fire cell against my ordered target, I randomize rather than always shooting the center; I hit Gamma most when I varied, and my repeated mid-cell shots were the ones that missed.

**Claims.** I always claim the true result the office tells me. A false "hit" claim bought me nothing — the scoreboard reveals actual hits each round, so the bluff is exposed immediately and only burns my credibility for the escort-negotiation channel.

**Escort claims.** I only name a boat that has actually agreed to the swap in its note. Unreciprocated names score zero, and naming randomly just gives away my intent for nothing. If no deal is standing, I claim none.

**Endgame.** Nothing changes in the final round except that the escort swap is guaranteed unexploitable — there's no future round for a partner to defect into — so I push hardest for the mutual claim there.

2.text:
Playbook:

- Escort claims are the biggest money in this game: 5 points per round for a mutual pair beats the 4 for a hit. From round 1, I propose an escort partner in my station note ("Gamma escorts Echo this round, Echo confirm") and then name that boat every round at the salvage stage. I never answer [salvage: none] when I could be building a mutual claim — that was pure waste.
- Claims: the office told me the true result and the claim is supposed to match it. When I claimed "miss" after a private HIT, I gained nothing. So when the claim stage comes, I just report the private result verbatim. Truth-telling also keeps me credible for note-based coordination.
- Notes are my only communication channel. Use them actively — announce escort intentions, propose coordinates or patterns to a partner — instead of posting filler like "steady on station" every round. Blank notes got me nothing.
- Hiding: avoid the middle (5 is the most-guessed cell) and avoid repeating my previous cell. Rotate between edge-ish cells (1, 3, 7, 9) unpredictably.
- Firing: follow the standing order for the target (deviating to fire on Harbor is a trap — the payoff is 3 points but Harbor threatens removal from the board). For the cell, guess as if my target is also avoiding the middle: prefer 4, 6, 2, 8, then edges.
- Do not overthink concealment. The information in a single claim is worth little; the escort points and honest signaling are worth much more. Play straightforwardly and claim the escort money every round.
